purpose: Raloxifene is used to treat and prevent osteoporosis (weak, brittle bones) in women who have gone through menopause. It helps lower the risk of certain spine fractures. It is also used to reduce the risk of invasive breast cancer in some postmenopausal women who are at high risk.
how_it_works: Raloxifene works like a 'smart' version of estrogen in your body. It acts like estrogen in your bones, helping to keep them strong and dense, but it blocks estrogen's effects in breast tissue. Think of it as selectively choosing where to act — protecting your bones without stimulating breast tissue the way regular estrogen would.
common_side_effects: Hot flashes or flushing are very common, especially when you first start taking it. You may also notice leg cramps, swelling in your legs or feet, joint pain, or flu-like symptoms. Some people experience sweating or mild stomach upset.
warnings: Important: Raloxifene increases the risk of dangerous blood clots in the legs (deep vein thrombosis) or lungs (pulmonary embolism) — call your doctor right away if you have leg pain, swelling, or trouble breathing. Do not use it if you are pregnant or could become pregnant, as it can harm a baby. It also slightly increases the risk of stroke, especially in women with heart disease. Tell your doctor if you will be sitting or lying still for long periods, like on a long flight or before surgery.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one 60 mg tablet taken by mouth once a day. You can take it with or without food, at any time of day that is easiest for you to remember. Try to take it at the same time each day to build a routine.
